To arrive at this single point estimate, I combined the most current data available on global giraffe populations with biological estimates regarding the number of spots per individual.

According to the Giraffe Conservation Foundation (GCF) and recent IUCN assessments (2022–2023), the total wild giraffe population has recovered slightly from previous lows.
*   **Wild Population:** Approximately 117,000 individuals.

**2. Average Spots Per Giraffe ($S$)**
The number of spots varies significantly by subspecies (e.g., Reticulated vs. Masai vs. Rothschild's), the definition of a "spot" (including leg speckles vs. only body patches), and the age of the animal (calves have fewer/darker spots that merge as they age).

**3. Final Calculation**
$$ \text{Total Spots} = \text{Total Population} \times \text{Average Spots} $$
